tool_input.description: Probe for infinite loop with astral-only codepoint range and count=1

result:
I created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/RandomStringUtilsAgentTest.java` with 59 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering `RandomStringUtils`'s static/instance methods, singleton accessors, length/charset guarantees, and boundary/error conditions.

58 tests pass. One test fails, and it reveals a genuine bug:

- **`testRandomAstralOnlyRangeWithCountOneDoesNotHang`** — `RandomStringUtils.secure().next(1, 0x10000, 0x10001, false, false)` hangs forever (confirmed via a timed-out background thread). The range `[0x10000, 0x10001)` contains exactly one code point, which needs a surrogate pair (2 chars). Since `count == 1` never has room for a 2-char code point, the rejection-sampling loop in `random(...)` (`RandomStringUtils.java`) keeps incrementing `count` back and retrying the same code point indefinitely instead of raising an error or terminating. Any single-character request restricted to a supplementary-plane-only range triggers this infinite loop.
